title: Signed and coefficient-natural substitution in actual derived internal Hom
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\ge1$, and coefficients are $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Integral operations are the specified completed operations, and field operations their rationalized and common-finite-stage forms. Use the actual operation datum, without assuming a full axiomatized six-functor package.
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and write $D^b_{ctf}$ for the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $H_A(M,U)=R\mathcal Hom_{X,A}(M,U)$ for the actual derived internal Hom [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and $J_U(M)=Rf_{A*}H_A(M,U)$, in the ambient derived realization of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. For $M,U,V\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and an isomorphism $c:U\xrightarrow{\sim}V$, put $j_c(M)=Rf_{A*}H_A(1_M,c)$. These components form a natural isomorphism of contravariant functors in $M$. With cohomological convention $P[r]^i=P^{i+r}$, $d_{P[r]}=(-1)^r d_P$, use the signed source-shift isomorphism
$$s_U(M,r):J_U(M[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}J_U(M)[-r],$$
normalized on a degree-$d$ Hom family by reindexing and multiplier $(-1)^{rd}$, and the derived direct-image shift comparison. Then, for every $r\in\mathbf Z$,
$$s_V(M,r)\circ j_c(M[r])=j_c(M)[-r]\circ s_U(M,r).$$
For a stipulated coefficient change $A\to B$, let $C_X,C_Y$ be the actual coefficient functors and
$$h_{M,U}:C_XH_A(M,U)\longrightarrow H_B(C_XM,C_XU),\qquad \gamma_Z:C_YRf_{A*}Z\longrightarrow Rf_{B*}C_XZ$$
its canonical internal-Hom and ordinary-image comparisons. Here $h$ is the transpose of coefficient-changed evaluation with the tensor comparison inserted; $\gamma$ is the mate of the pullback comparison. Take $U',V'\in D^b_{ctf}(X,B)$ and isomorphisms $u:C_XU\to U'$, $v:C_XV\to V'$, $c':U'\to V'$ such that $v\circ C_Xc=c'\circ u$. Set
$$\sigma_{U,u}(M)=Rf_{B*}\bigl(H_B(1,u)\circ h_{M,U}\bigr)\circ\gamma_{H_A(M,U)},$$
and define $\sigma_{V,v}$ by the same formula. Then
$$\sigma_{V,v}(M)\circ C_Y(j_c(M))=j_{c'}(C_XM)\circ\sigma_{U,u}(M).$$
This is a commutative square of the specified maps on their stated domains in the ambient derived realization; it does not require $h$ or $\gamma$ to be isomorphisms. At integral coefficients use completed realizations and at field stages their specified scalar transports. No biduality or full six-functor-package axiom is assumed.

proof.text: Write $a^*_U=H_A(a,1_U)$ for a morphism $a:M'\to M$. Bifunctoriality gives $H_A(a,1_V)H_A(1_M,c)=H_A(1_{M'},c)H_A(a,1_U)$. Apply $Rf_{A*}$ to obtain the naturality square for $j_c$. The inverse component is $Rf_{A*}H_A(1_M,c^{-1})$: both composites are identities by functoriality. These are ambient derived-category maps; this argument does not assert constructibility of their values.

proof.text: Fix a complex $L$ representing $M$ and use the functorial K-injective representatives $I(U),I(V)$ of derived Hom. For a chain map $b:I(U)\to I(V)$, the signed reindexing $s$ sends a degree-$d$ family $\phi$ on $L[r]$ to the family $(-1)^{rd}\phi^{j-r}$ at index $j$ on $L$. Thus $s(b\phi)^j=(-1)^{rd}b^{j+d-r}\phi^{j-r}=b^{j+d-r}(s\phi)^j$. This is equality after every Hom-product projection. The Hom-complex shift lemma supplies the chain isomorphism, with inverse reindexing and the same sign; this calculation checks its specified normalization and target naturality. Quasi-isomorphism invariance of the representative construction and the localization universal property descend this natural square to every derived morphism $c$, including inverses of quasi-isomorphisms. Consequently $s^H_V H_A(1_{M[r]},c)=H_A(1_M,c)[-r]s^H_U$ for actual derived Hom, over the finite coefficient sheaf or the completed integral coefficient sheaf. The latter Hom is computed in that ambient module category, so no term of the K-injective resolution is required to be constructible.

proof.text: Apply $Rf_{A*}$ to the square in step 2 and compose with its natural comparison $Rf_{A*}(Z[-r])\cong(Rf_{A*}Z)[-r]$. Naturality of this comparison gives precisely $s_V j_c(M[r])=j_c(M)[-r]s_U$. At finite level the right-derived-functor shift lemma gives the comparison. At integral level $Rf_*$ is the specified derived limit of the finite direct images, and the levelwise comparisons are only derived-category isomorphisms, not strict tower maps. The integral direct-image shift lemma gives a comparison $\theta_{Z,-r}$ natural in every derived morphism $Z\to Z'$, in particular in $H_A(1_M,c)[-r]$ for the completed integral Hom; its naturality gives the square. At $E$, apply the rationalized operations and their stated bilinear action on morphisms to the same identity; at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, represent the finitely many objects and arrows over a common finite field stage and apply the same equation there. The operation's comparison isomorphisms cancel at intermediate objects. Thus every stipulated coefficient stage has the same signed equation.

proof.text:
Set $F=C_X$ and $a=H_A(1_M,c)$. Let $\mathrm{ev}_U:H_A(M,U)\otimes M\to U$ be evaluation, with its stipulated tensor convention. If $t_U:FH_A(M,U)\otimes FM\to F(H_A(M,U)\otimes M)$ denotes the tensor comparison inserted in the definition of $h$, its uncurried map is $e_U=F(\mathrm{ev}_U)t_U$. Evaluation naturality says $\mathrm{ev}_V(a\otimes1)=c\,\mathrm{ev}_U$. Tensor-comparison naturality therefore gives $e_V(Fa\otimes1)=F(c)e_U$. Transpose this equality under the tensor-Hom adjunction in the $B$ realization, using the adjunction transpose-square lemma. Since $h$ is this very transpose, it yields
$$h_{M,V}F(a)=H_B(1_{FM},F(c))h_{M,U}.$$
This uses no inverse of $t$ or $h$. The argument takes place on the stipulated domains of these transposes, so also applies to the specified completed evaluation and tensor comparison; it does not replace them by ordinary tensor operations. The representative model supplies the actual ambient evaluation, and transposing its natural square is the same formal calculation in each realization.

proof.text:
Put $G=Rf_{A*}$ and $G'=Rf_{B*}$. The stipulated $\gamma:C_YG\to G'C_X$ is the mate natural transformation. In the component formula for a mate, every factor is a whiskered unit, pullback comparison, or counit, hence a natural transformation. Their naturality squares paste. Evaluating that square at the particular arrow $a=H_A(1_M,c)$ gives
$$\gamma_{H_A(M,V)}C_Y(Ga)=G'(C_Xa)\gamma_{H_A(M,U)}.$$
This proves the needed equation for the specified mate, regardless of whether any component is invertible.

proof.text:
Abbreviate $h_U=h_{M,U}$, $h_V=h_{M,V}$, and $\gamma_U=\gamma_{H_A(M,U)}$. Expand the specified $\sigma$ and use step 5, then step 4:
$$\begin{aligned}
\sigma_{V,v}C_Y(j_c(M))
&=G'(H_B(1,v)h_V)G'(C_Xa)\gamma_U\\
&=G'(H_B(1,v)H_B(1,C_Xc)h_U)\gamma_U\\
&=G'(H_B(1,v\circ C_Xc)h_U)\gamma_U\\
&=G'(H_B(1,c'\circ u)h_U)\gamma_U\\
&=G'H_B(1,c')\,G'(H_B(1,u)h_U)\gamma_U\\
&=j_{c'}(C_XM)\sigma_{U,u}(M).
\end{aligned}$$
The fourth line is exactly the hypothesis $v\circ C_Xc=c'\circ u$; the other rearrangements are functoriality and associativity. This equality is in the given $B$ realization. Completed functors and field-stage scalar transports already occur in its factors, so the same calculation proves their squares without a limit-detection assertion. Neither biduality nor an axiomatized six-functor package occurs.
